subject.title: Feature: Subscribe to WhatsApp call events (Baileys)

question: Should OpenClaw add opt-in inbound WhatsApp Baileys call-event tracking, and which sanitized surface should expose that activity to agents or plugins?
rationale: The missing listener is clear, but call metadata affects privacy, access control, retention, and agent/plugin visibility, so automation should not choose the permanent exposure model.

options.title: Approve Opt-In Plugin Tracking
options.body: Add a default-off WhatsApp plugin listener for Baileys call events, sanitize and filter metadata like inbound messages, and expose contact activity through one documented surface.

options.title: Design Exposure Surface First
options.body: Keep the issue open while maintainers decide whether the event belongs in plugin hooks, session metadata, a contact-activity store, or a query/tool surface.

options.title: Decline Inbound Call Tracking
options.body: Close the direction if OpenClaw should avoid storing or exposing WhatsApp call metadata even when Baileys emits it.

recommendation.title: Approve Opt-In Plugin Tracking
recommendation.body: Add a default-off WhatsApp plugin listener for Baileys call events, sanitize and filter metadata like inbound messages, and expose contact activity through one documented surface.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent WhatsApp call-surface history and already scoped this as WhatsApp-plugin-owned work.
